name: Emeka Garcia

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am a senior researcher with the Work Futures Panel, independent of employers, AI firms, unions and government. Your answers are confidential. Tell me about an ordinary workday.

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am 43 and prepare accounts and tax returns at a firm, often for small building contractors. I have a bachelor’s degree and a professional accountancy qualification, and I know the usual jobs, though hard tax cases still go to a senior. I use an AI tool now and then after a colleague tests it, but I still want the bank statement beside the draft. I like settling a builder’s disputed equipment charge, but late bundles of hire receipts make filing week drag.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: What is home like after work?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: Inez, my partner, works shifts at a food depot, and we have two school-age children and a mortgage. My pay is low for an experienced accountant; we have less than a month of expenses saved. Only a few similar firms are nearby, so I prefer learning a proven method while keeping paid hours.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say a quicker routine check might help us clear the tax queue, as long as the senior still signs the return. Clients want a person to answer their questions.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The mortgage and school bills press on my below-normal accountant pay. We have less than a month saved, so even an ordinary sick week can put us behind without any AI change.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would keep preparing the builders’ accounts and tax returns with the checklist our firm uses. I would pack lunch three days a week and transfer the 18 I save into a separate bill account each Friday while my hours hold; I would carry that on through the first year.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the bills, not about this small software change. A quiet month at the firm already makes me check the bank app twice.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Which client question takes your time?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A builder brought three receipts for the same hire machine and could not remember which was paid. I checked the bank statement with him before filing, because a quick total alone would be wrong.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What does the bill account cover first?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The mortgage, then the children’s school meals. My partner Inez works shifts at a food depot, but we do not count an extra shift until it is on the rota.

say: I would welcome a **quicker check** if a person still signs returns.
I would remind clients we can **answer questions** about their figures.
think: Our **mortgage and school bills** already strain my low pay.
Less than **one month saved** makes a sick week dangerous.
do: Keep preparing **builders’ accounts** and tax returns with the firm checklist.
Pack **three lunches weekly** and transfer 18 into the bill account while hours hold.
feel: I feel **anxious** about existing bills despite little AI change.
S0.quote: A quiet month at the firm already makes me check the bank app twice.
fieldNote: His **baseline anxiety** comes from mortgage and school costs on low pay, even if technology changes little.
He ties a **real weekly deposit** to lunches he no longer buys and does not budget his partner’s unconfirmed shifts.

steps.text: Keep preparing builders’ accounts and returns with firm checklist
Transfer 18 from packed lunches to bill account weekly while hours hold

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the firm to show which tax checks software will take and who still reviews a builder’s messy papers. A new tool should earn its place on real files.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Writing notes and checking accounts are much of my paid day, so I expect the firm to cut a large part of my hours if software takes those tasks. With less than a month saved and few nearby firms, a big wage loss would keep me awake.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask my senior reviewer to let me test the approved draft checker on four closed returns during paid hours after she shows it works. I would cancel our paid sports streaming and add 20 monthly to the bill account; if my hours fall in the first year, I would apply for an advertised local account-clerk post only with written pay and hours no lower than now, keeping current shifts until an offer and start date.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed by the likely wage cut, even though I can learn a tested tool. Our family cannot pay the lender with a training certificate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you check in those four returns?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would compare the draft tax figures with the bank statements and the builder’s receipts, then ask the senior to review my error list. I use AI now and then, but only after someone else has checked a process.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the clerk post has fewer hours?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would stay on the paid work I have while looking at another posted job. A smaller title is fine, but fewer paid hours would make the mortgage problem worse.

say: I would ask which **tax checks** software replaces and who reviews messy papers.
I would make the **approved tool** prove itself on closed files.
think: I expect a **large cut** in my writing and checking hours.
A **thin reserve** and few nearby firms make that loss frightening.
do: Test **four closed returns** with approved drafting tool after senior demonstration during paid hours.
Cancel **sports streaming** and deposit 20 monthly in bill account.
After lost hours, apply for **advertised clerk work** with written equal pay and hours; retain shifts until start date.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by expected lost pay and a fixed mortgage.
S1.quote: Our family cannot pay the lender with a training certificate.
fieldNote: His **expected hours loss** is large enough to threaten mortgage payments, with almost no reserve or local job market.
He accepts **tested AI** under senior review but will not move to a clerk post with fewer paid hours.

steps.text: Test four closed returns with approved tool after paid senior demonstration
Deposit 20 monthly from cancelled streaming into bill account
Apply for advertised clerk post after cuts with written equal pay/hours; retain shifts until start date

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the firm AGI by 2028 reaches the accounts and tax screens in 2028, before capable robots around 2031. We need written notice of cuts while we can still plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect most of my work on returns and accounts to go when cheaper AGI can do the thinking. Less than one month in savings would not cover the mortgage, and the few local firms may be cutting too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask for written cut dates and stop the children’s paid weekend club at the next renewal, keeping the fee for the mortgage. If my hours fall in the first year after 2028, I would apply for advertised local account-clerk posts with written pay and hours at least equal to my current job; if no offer arrives, I would ask Inez whether confirmed depot shifts can cover one mortgage payment while I keep any paid return work. The weekend club is football while I am already at home, so cancelling it does not remove childcare.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel alarmed and lie awake thinking of a missed payment. I have a phone list, but it does not put wages in our account.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could Inez take those shifts?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Inez sometimes covers a weekend shift at the food depot, but the supervisor may give it to someone else. We would budget the money only after the rota and paid rate are confirmed and someone can collect the children.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave the firm quickly?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No, I would keep every paid return hour until a local employer offers written salary and a start date. I cannot turn a possible vacancy into next month’s mortgage.

say: I would say **AGI by 2028** reaches our tax screens before capable robots.
I would ask for **written cut dates** before the rota changes.
think: I expect most of my **accounts and return work** to go in 2028.
Our **sub-month cushion** cannot cover the mortgage through a job search.
do: Stop paying for the children’s **weekend club** at renewal and retain its fee.
After lost hours, apply to **advertised local clerk posts** with written equal pay and hours; retain return shifts until start date.
If no offer arrives, ask **partner Inez** about confirmed depot shifts and childcare for one mortgage payment.
feel: I feel **alarmed** by expected wage loss and a missed mortgage payment.
S2.quote: I cannot turn a possible vacancy into next month’s mortgage.
fieldNote: His **desk exposure** starts with AGI in 2028, three years before capable robots affect hands-on work.
He will keep **paid return hours** during the search and count Inez’s depot income only after rate, rota and childcare are confirmed.

steps.text: Stop children’s weekend club at renewal and retain fee for mortgage
Apply to advertised clerk posts after cuts with written equal pay/hours; retain shifts until start date
Ask partner Inez about confirmed depot rate, rota and childcare if no offer arrives

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say AGI by 2031 gives us a few years to learn what the firm will still pay for. The robots around 2034 do not delay the tax desk problem.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Five years might let us build a small cushion and learn work with clients, but we are starting with very little cash. I still expect routine returns to shrink sharply in 2031.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would ask the partner to fund a short course in payroll reconciliation, which means checking wage totals against the bank, with paid study hours. I would enrol only after fees and paid time are approved in writing; I would save 45 monthly while both wages hold, and in the first year after 2031, if my return hours fall, I would take a vacant paid payroll post only with written salary and hours no worse than now, or keep remaining return hours while applying for posted local work. I would keep any current paid work until the replacement start date is confirmed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious because the plan depends on both wages and employer funding. I can see more time than in 2028, but not spare tuition money.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the course is refused?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask the senior reviewer to let me practise wage reconciliations on old files during current paid hours if she agrees. I would keep preparing returns rather than spend the mortgage money on tuition.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why payroll rather than tax advice?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I have checked wage totals for builder clients before, though I still need supervision. Payroll may be another paid task in the firm, but I would not call it safe from AGI.

say: I would ask for **paid payroll training** before 2031.
I would remind staff the **2034 robots** do not postpone tax desk risk.
think: Routine **return work** may shrink sharply in 2031 despite my years of experience.
Our **thin starting cushion** limits self-funded training.
do: Enrol in **firm-funded payroll training** with written fees and paid hours; otherwise keep returns and practise old wages with approved paid supervision.
Save **45 monthly** while both wages hold.
Take a **vacant paid payroll post** after cuts only with written equal pay/hours and confirmed start; otherwise search while retaining paid accounts.
feel: I feel **anxious** about funding and both household wages.
S3.quote: I would keep preparing returns rather than spend the mortgage money on tuition.
fieldNote: He defines **payroll reconciliation** in plain language and has limited exposure through builder clients, rather than claiming mastery.
His **funding fallback** is supervised practice on old files during paid hours; an internal move requires a vacancy and written equal terms.

steps.text: Enrol with written firm-funded fees and paid hours; otherwise practise old wages with approved paid supervision
Save 45 monthly while both household wages hold
Take vacant paid payroll after cuts with written equal pay/hours, confirmed start; otherwise search while employed
Keep current paid returns if firm refuses payroll course

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say AGI by 2036 gives our family time to reduce debt and the firm time to train staff. The tax screens still change in 2036, before capable robots around 2039.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Ten years might see the children finish school and a larger cash cushion if both wages stay steady. I still expect much of my return preparation to go in 2036, even if I become better at the job.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now I would keep reviewing builder accounts and ask the senior reviewer for one paid supervised payroll file each month if the manager approves. I would build a three-month cash reserve first, then pay 70 monthly against the mortgage principal while both wages hold; in the first year after 2036, if return hours fall, I would take a vacant payroll post only with written equal salary and hours, or keep remaining paid accounts work while applying to advertised local firms. I would keep any current paid work until the replacement start date is confirmed.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I feel anxious about the mortgage we have now, although the longer clock helps. I would need steady pay to make the savings plan real.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if no monthly payroll file is available?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the account files I already have and wait for a paid supervised opening. I would not call unpaid evenings a training plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you depend on family for money?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Our relatives can collect the children in an emergency, but I would not build a ten-year budget on gifts. I want the mortgage paid from wages we can actually see.

say: I would use **ten years** to train and lower mortgage debt.
I would note **2039 robots** arrive after tax screen changes.
think: Much **return preparation** may end when thinking AGI arrives in 2036.
A **three-month reserve** needs both wages to continue.
do: Keep **builder accounts** and learn on paid supervised payroll files only with manager approval.
Build **three months cash**, then pay 70 monthly against principal while both wages hold.
Take a **vacant paid payroll post** after cuts only with written equal pay/hours and confirmed start; otherwise search while retaining paid accounts.
feel: I feel **anxious** about today’s mortgage despite a longer preparation window.
S4.quote: I would not call unpaid evenings a training plan.
fieldNote: His **present thin cushion** keeps the mortgage worrying even in a ten-year AGI world.
He keeps **current account work** if supervised payroll files are unavailable, and only moves to a paid vacancy with written equal terms.

steps.text: Learn payroll on paid supervised monthly files only if manager approves
Build three months cash then pay 70 monthly against mortgage while both wages hold
Take vacant paid payroll after cuts with written equal pay/hours, confirmed start; otherwise search while employed
Keep paid builder accounts if no supervised payroll file opens

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help you if it happened?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because our mortgage cannot survive losing most of my return hours. Written cut notice, employer-paid training and an actual paid vacancy would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I didn't ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: You did not ask how many paydays a mortgage can wait. An empty desk in the accounts room would reach our kitchen before anyone finished a staffing memo.

headlineQuote: An empty desk in the accounts room would reach our kitchen before anyone finished a staffing memo.
portrait: At **43**, Emeka is an experienced accountant with a bachelor’s degree and professional qualification who handles building-contractor files.
He and **partner Inez** have two school-age children, a mortgage, low pay and less than one month saved.
He uses **AI occasionally** after colleagues test it, and few similar jobs are nearby.
The **2028 deadline** threatens his return hours; longer runways allow funded payroll learning and conditional mortgage savings.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could remove most of his return hours before the household can cover one mortgage payment.
whatWouldHelp: He wants **written notice**, employer-paid training and a real paid vacancy with protected hours.
